slides.headline: The dairy swap was easy. The steps changed.
slides.photo_label: Stock photo of the original dairy recipe, not the adapted dish

slides.headline: The list was the easy part
More chicken did not mean longer broiling
slides.rewrite: Two batches, 8 to 10 minutes per batch
slides.why: Uncrowded chicken keeps the char that balances the creamy sauce
slides.as_written: Spread it on a foil-lined baking sheet. Broil for 8 to 10 minutes.

slides.headline: Do not multiply the simmer
slides.rewrite: Check at 10 minutes. Done when a spoon leaves a trail
slides.why: A wider pan evaporates liquid faster
slides.as_written: Cook uncovered for 10 to 12 minutes, until the sauce leaves a trail.

slides.headline: Why the drip matters more now
slides.rewrite: With coconut yogurt, let the excess drip off
slides.why: The coating chars rather than pools
slides.as_written: Lift the chicken from the marinade, letting the excess drip off.

slides.headline: Simmer gently, then check the chicken
slides.rewrite: Whisk smooth, simmer gently, check several pieces
slides.why: Separated coconut cream smooths out; chicken still has to reach 165°F
slides.as_written: Stir the cream into the sauce. Simmer gently for 5 minutes.

caption:
One swap can move the whole method. In this dairy-free chicken tikka masala, scaled from 4 to 6 servings, the ingredient list is simple: coconut yogurt, vegan butter, coconut cream. The steps are where cooks get burned. More chicken needs more broiler space, not a longer blast. A wider pan means you start checking the sauce at 10 minutes and stop when a spoon dragged through leaves a clear trail. Coconut cream wants a gentle simmer. Chicken still needs 165°F in the thickest pieces. This is a real RecipeFix result, so the changed step comes with the reason.
